fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. The LORD doesn't tell David to wait. He answers, “Go up.” That's a clear yes to David's question.
Bethlehem is a good guess, friend. But the text never sends David there. The LORD replies, “To Hebron.” That's the town David heads for.
Keilah isn't the town the LORD names here. David asks where he should go, and the LORD replies, “To Hebron.” One question, one town, no detours.

Jesse and his brothers aren't named in this move. The passage names two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel. Then it adds the men who were with David and their households. Look at that list, friend, and keep the names straight.

Samuel isn't named in this move. The text says David went with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. His men and their households come next. Priests aren't on the list, and I checked it twice, like a baker with a timer.
Yes, baker! The text says, “…there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.” They come to Hebron and make it official. That's the big moment here.
Good try, but there's no crown handoff in these verses. The men of Judah anoint David king over the house of Judah, right there in Hebron. The text only tells us about anointing, not a crown.
That's right! The men of Judah tell David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.” That's a heavy piece of news. After it, the text says David sent messengers to those men.

Ziklag is not the town in this verse. The men of Judah tell David it was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul. It's a tricky name, and I once mixed up two sprinkle jars myself. The name to hold on to is Jabesh-gilead.

Judah isn't the word for this blank, friend. The text says Ish-bosheth is made king “…over all Israel.” In the same passage, the house of Judah anointed David and followed him. Two different groups are going two different ways.
Moab isn't in this verse. Abner makes Ish-bosheth king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin, “…over all Israel.” Israel is the word that finishes the sentence.

You've got the six months, but the years are off. The text says David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah for seven years and six months. Ish-bosheth reigns two years, so David's time in Hebron is a good deal longer.
